user.text: Migrate every route and file from the Pages Router to the Next.js App Router. When finished, remove the pages dir entirely. Ensure the proper App Router APIs are used. If a Pages Router API was used that no longer exists in App Router, replace it with the newer version or the new pattern. Make sure to add types.

history.assistant:
Every route is now on the App Router and pages/ is gone. The production build and the TypeScript check both pass, and the routes worked when I ran them against the built app.

Migrated routes:
- _app.js and _document.js → app/layout.tsx. The header, nav, footer and global CSS moved here. The <Head> tags became a typed metadata export, and the Google Fonts <link> tags became next/font/google (Inter).
- index.js → app/page.tsx. getServerSideProps was replaced by an async Server Component. req.headers became await headers(), and the fetch uses cache: 'no-store' so it still runs on every request.
- blog/index.js → app/blog/page.tsx. getStaticProps with revalidate: 60 became fetch(..., { next: { revalidate: 60 } }).
- blog/[id].js → app/blog/[id]/page.tsx:
  - getStaticPaths became generateStaticParams.
  - fallback: 'blocking' became dynamicParams = true.
  - The 5-minute revalidate moved onto the fetch calls.
  - notFound: true became notFound().
  - The <Head> tags became generateMetadata.
  - router.isFallback was removed from App Router, so I added app/blog/[id]/loading.tsx to show the loading state.
  - The page is typed with PageProps<'/blog/[id]'>.
- 404.js → app/not-found.tsx.
- _error.js → app/error.tsx plus app/global-error.tsx, which catches errors in the root layout itself. getInitialProps doesn't exist in App Router, so these use the error and retry props instead.
- api/posts/index.js and api/posts/[id].js → app/api/posts/route.ts and app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts. Each HTTP method has its own typed handler using NextRequest, NextResponse and RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>. The manual 405 check is gone because Next.js now returns 405 for unsupported methods itself.

Supporting files:
- next/router's useRouter was replaced with the one from next/navigation. It now lives in two small client components, components/NavigateButton.tsx and components/BackButton.tsx, so the pages themselves can stay Server Components.
- Plain <a> tags for internal links are now <Link>.
- components/AppProvider.js became AppProvider.tsx, marked 'use client', with a typed context.
- lib/types.ts holds the shared Post and Comment types.

Checks run:
- npx next typegen && npx tsc --noEmit: exit 0.
- npx next build: succeeded. / renders on each request, /blog revalidates every 1 minute, and /blog/[id] prerendered 10 posts that revalidate every 5 minutes.
- next start with curl:
  - GET /api/posts returned the list.
  - POST with missing fields returned 400; a valid POST returned 201.
  - PUT and DELETE on /api/posts/7 worked.
  - PATCH returned 405.
  - An unknown URL returned 404.
  - /blog/3 has the right <title>, and / shows the user agent.

next typegen reformatted tsconfig.json and added .next/dev/types//.ts to include. .next/ and next-env.d.ts aren't in .gitignore, so they show up as untracked files. I didn't touch your existing package.json change.

exit_code=0 `error.js` wraps a route segment and its nested children in a [React Error Boundary](https://react.dev/reference/react/Component#catching-rendering-errors-with-an-error-boundary). When an error throws within the boundary, the `error` component shows as the fallback UI. > **Good to know**: > > - The [React DevTools](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools) allow you to toggle error boundaries to test error states. > - If you want errors to bubble up to the parent error boundary, you can `throw` when rendering the `error` component. > - For component-level error recovery that aren't tied to route segments like [`error.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error), use the [`catchError`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/catchError) function. In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `error.js` wraps `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, `page.js`, and nested `layout.js` files in a React error boundary. It does **not** wrap the `layout.js` or `template.js` above it in the same segment. To handle errors in the root layout, use [`global-error.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error#global-error). ## Reference ### Props #### `error` An instance of an [`Error`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Error) object forwarded to the `error.js` Client Component. > **Good to know:** During development, the `Error` object forwarded to the client will be serialized and include the `message` of the original error for easier debugging. However, **this behavior is different in production** to avoid leaking potentially sensitive details included in the error to the client. #### `error.message` - Errors forwarded from Client Components show the original `Error` message. - Errors forwarded from Server Components show a generic message with an identifier. This is to prevent leaking sensitive details. You can use the identifier, under `error.digest`, to match the corresponding server-side logs. #### `error.digest` An automatically generated hash of the error thrown. It can be used to match the corresponding error in server-side logs. #### `retry` The cause of an error can sometimes be temporary. In these cases, trying again might resolve the issue. An error component can use the `retry()` function to prompt the user to attempt to recover from the error. When executed, the function will try to re-fetch and re-render the error boundary's children.
